# Tellers OTIO timeline reference

A tellers timeline is an [OpenTimelineIO](https://opentimelineio.readthedocs.io) JSON document with extra data under `metadata["tellers.ai"]` and in tellers effects. New to the format? Start with the [reading guide](reading-otio.md).

- [Objects](#objects)
- [Tellers effects](#tellers-effects)

## Objects

### Timeline

The document. Its `tracks` stack holds every track; timeline-wide settings (fonts) live in its `metadata["tellers.ai"]`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Timeline.1"` | Always `Timeline.1`. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai.availableFonts` lists the fonts text clips may use. The player also reads `tellers.ai.groups[<group_id>].parameters` (a keyframable transform of a clip group: `x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity`, …, edited with the clip-group API) and the top-level `tellers_aspect_ratio` (`16_9`, `9_16`, …), which this library keeps as plain metadata, with no typed API. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `tracks` | [Stack](#stack) |  |  | The stack of every track. |

### Stack

The tracks of the timeline, composited together. Tracks render in list order: the first is the bottom layer, the last the top one (painter's order). Of its `effects`, the player applies `ColorLut`s to the whole composited image and uses a `MotionBlur` as every clip's default; it ignores the others there. The player also reads `enabled: false` on this stack (nothing plays), a field this library drops on load.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Stack.1"` | Always `Stack.1`. |
| `children` | array of [Track](#track) |  |  | The tracks, bottom layer first. |
| `effects` | array of [Effect](#effect) |  |  | The timeline stage: `ColorLut`s grade the whole composited image and a `MotionBlur` is every clip's default; the player applies no other effect here. |
| `markers` | array of [Marker](#marker) |  |  | Timeline markers, in timeline time. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |

### Track

A row of items played one after the other: each item starts where the previous one ends, so a track's timing is the sum of its items' durations. Video tracks carry picture only and audio tracks sound only.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Track.1"` | Always `Track.1`. |
| `children` | array of [Item](#item) |  |  | The items, in play order. |
| `effects` | array of [Effect](#effect) |  |  | Effects applied to each clip of the track (the track stage). |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | `true` | A disabled track is neither drawn nor heard. |
| `kind` | [TrackKind](#trackkind) | yes |  | `video`, `audio` or `other`. |
| `markers` | array of [Marker](#marker) |  |  | Track markers, in timeline time. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai.timeline_id` is the track id; `tellers.ai.created_by: "auto"` marks tracks the library created. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name, e.g. `V1` or `A2`. |

### TrackKind

What a track carries. Read case-insensitively (`Video` and `video` both parse); written lowercase.

Values: `"video"` \| `"audio"` \| `"other"`.

### Item

An entry of a track: a clip, a gap of empty time, a composite clip, or a transition between two neighbours.

One of [Clip](#clip), [Gap](#gap), [CompositeStack](#compositestack), [Transition](#transition).

### Clip

A piece of media (or generated content) placed on a track for the duration of its `source_range`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Clip.2"` | `Clip.2` (`Clip.1` is read too). |
| `active_media_reference_key` | string \| null |  |  | Which `media_references` entry plays; `DEFAULT_MEDIA` when unset. |
| `effects` | array of [Effect](#effect) |  |  | Effects applied to this clip only (the clip stage), in order. |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | `true` | A disabled clip is neither drawn nor heard; it still takes its time. |
| `markers` | array of [Marker](#marker) |  |  | Clip markers, in source (media) time. |
| `media_references` | map of string → [MediaReference](#mediareference) |  |  | The clip's media, by key; usually a single `DEFAULT_MEDIA`. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai.timeline_id` is the item id, `tellers.ai.group_id` names the player group whose transform applies (see the timeline's `tellers.ai.groups`), `tellers.ai["Tellers Group ID"]` is this library's edit group, and the Resolve `Link Group ID` ties a video to its audio (sync partners). |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `source_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) | yes |  | The part of the media played: `start_time` in the media's own time, and `duration`, which is also how long the clip lasts on the track. |

### Gap

Empty time on a track: nothing is drawn or heard for its duration.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Gap.1"` | `Gap.1`. |
| `effects` | array of [Effect](#effect) |  |  | Kept for OTIO round trips; nothing applies them. |
| `markers` | array of [Marker](#marker) |  |  | Kept for OTIO round trips; the API places no markers on gaps. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai.timeline_id` is the item id. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `source_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) | yes |  | Only `duration` matters: how long the gap lasts. |

### CompositeStack

A composite clip: a `Stack.1` nested inside a video track, drawn as one clip made of its own tracks. It lasts `source_range.duration` when a source range is set, otherwise as long as its longest child track.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Stack.1"` | `Stack.1`. |
| `children` | array of [Track](#track) |  |  | Its own tracks, bottom layer first, timed like the timeline's. |
| `effects` | array of [Effect](#effect) |  |  | Effects applied to the composite as a whole, like a clip's. |
| `enabled` | boolean \| null |  |  | A disabled composite is neither drawn nor heard; it still takes its time. |
| `markers` | array of [Marker](#marker) |  |  | Markers, kept for OTIO round trips. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai.timeline_id` is the item id. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `source_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) \| null |  |  | Optional. `start_time` is where in its child tracks it starts playing, and `duration` how long it lasts on the outer track. |

### Transition

A transition between the two items around it on a track. It takes no time of its own: it overlaps the end of the item before it by `in_offset` and the start of the item after it by `out_offset`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Transition.1"` | `Transition.1`. |
| `in_offset` | [RationalTime](#rationaltime) |  |  | How far it reaches back into the item before it. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai.parameters` holds the player's `color` (dips, `#000000` by default; `DipToBlack` / `DipToWhite` override it) and `direction` (`left`, `right`, `up`, `down`; `left` by default), read and written by `Transition::color` and `Transition::direction`. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `out_offset` | [RationalTime](#rationaltime) |  |  | How far it reaches into the item after it. |
| `transition_type` | string |  | `"SMPTE_Dissolve"` | OTIO's `SMPTE_Dissolve` (a dissolve) or `Custom_Transition`. The player also reads `Dissolve`, `CrossDissolve`, `DipToBlack`, `DipToWhite`, `DipToColor`, `Wipe`, `Push`, `Slide` and `Zoom`, compared without case or punctuation, and dissolves on anything else. `Transition::kind` / `set_kind` read and write it as a `TransitionKind`. Sound fades over every transition (a crossfade between two clips, a fade from or to silence next to a gap): `tellers.ai.audio-constant-power` (equal power) and `tellers.ai.audio-constant-gain` (linear) pick the curve, read and written by `Transition::audio_kind` / `set_audio_kind`; any other type fades at constant power between two clips and at constant gain from or to silence. Pictures draw an audio type as a dissolve. |

### MediaReference

What a clip plays, chosen by `OTIO_SCHEMA`. `MissingReference.1` is also accepted and read as an external reference with an empty `target_url` (and written back as `ExternalReference.1`); the player draws it as a gap.

#### `ExternalReference.1`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | `"ExternalReference.1"` | yes |  | Picks the kind of reference. |
| `available_image_bounds` | any JSON |  |  | OTIO image bounds; unused by the player. |
| `available_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) \| null |  |  | The time range the media file covers, in its own time; `source_range` stays inside it. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai` holds asset details such as the asset id. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `target_url` | string |  | `""` | URL of the media file. Resolved from the asset before playback and stripped before saving, so a stored timeline may have it empty. |

#### `GeneratorReference.1`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | `"GeneratorReference.1"` | yes |  | Picks the kind of reference. |
| `available_image_bounds` | any JSON |  |  | OTIO image bounds; unused by the player. |
| `available_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) \| null |  |  | The time range the media file covers, in its own time; `source_range` stays inside it. |
| `generator_kind` | string | yes |  | `Rich` (Resolve Rich Text: HTML), `Text` (plain text), `Shape` (rectangle, ellipse, line) or another generator. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | Free JSON. `tellers.ai` holds asset details such as the asset id. |
| `name` | string \| null |  |  | Display name. |
| `parameters` | [GeneratorParameters](#generatorparameters) |  |  | The generator's parameters; see GeneratorParameters. |

### GeneratorParameters

The parameters of a generator reference: a Resolve `Rich Text` block for `generator_kind: "Rich"`, or the player's own keys for `Text` and `Shape` generators (see the reading guide). Other keys are kept as they are.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Resolve_OTIO` | array of [ResolveOTIOEffect](#resolveotioeffect) \| null |  |  | Resolve effects of the generator: for Rich Text, a `Rich Text` effect with the `title blob` HTML, `position`, zoom and rotation. |

### Effect

An effect on a clip, a track or the stack. Tellers effects are named `tellers.ai.<Effect>` and keep their parameters in `metadata["tellers.ai"].parameters` (see [Tellers effects](#tellers-effects)); Resolve transforms and crop are `Resolve Effect`s with a `Resolve_OTIO` block, as is the legacy clip volume (read, never written: the volume is `tellers.ai.Volume`). Other OTIO keys (e.g. `time_scalar`) are kept as they are.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Effect.1"` | `Effect.1`; OTIO's `LinearTimeWarp.1` and `FreezeFrame.1` are read too. |
| `effect_name` | string |  | `""` | Which effect: `tellers.ai.<Effect>` for tellers effects, `Resolve Effect` for Resolve ones. |
| `enabled` | boolean \| null |  |  | `false` turns the effect off without removing it; absent means enabled. |
| `metadata` | [EffectMetadata](#effectmetadata) |  |  | Where the effect's settings live; see EffectMetadata. |
| `name` | string |  | `""` | Display label. |

### EffectMetadata

The metadata of an effect. Keys other than `Resolve_OTIO` (notably `tellers.ai`) are kept as they are.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Resolve_OTIO` | [ResolveOTIOEffect](#resolveotioeffect) \| null |  |  | The Resolve effect of a `Resolve Effect` (Transform, Cropping, legacy volume). |

### Marker

A note on a point or range of the edit. `marked_range` is in the time of the object holding it: timeline time on the stack and tracks, source (media) time on a clip.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"Marker.2"` | `Marker.2`. |
| `color` | string |  | `"RED"` | An OTIO marker color (`RED`, `GREEN`, `BLUE`, ...). |
| `comment` | string |  | `""` | Body of the note. |
| `marked_range` | [TimeRange](#timerange) |  |  | The flagged point (zero duration) or range. |
| `metadata` | any JSON |  |  | `tellers.ai.timeline_id` is the marker id, `tellers.ai.created_by` its author. |
| `name` | string |  | `""` | Title of the note. |

### TimeRange

A span of time: `start_time` and `duration`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"TimeRange.1"` | `TimeRange.1`. |
| `duration` | [RationalTime](#rationaltime) | yes |  | How long it lasts. |
| `start_time` | [RationalTime](#rationaltime) | yes |  | Where the range starts. |

### RationalTime

A time as `value / rate` seconds (e.g. `{ value: 48, rate: 24 }` is 2 s).

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OTIO_SCHEMA` | string |  | `"RationalTime.1"` | `RationalTime.1`. |
| `rate` | number | yes |  | Units per second, e.g. a frame rate (`1` for plain seconds). |
| `value` | number | yes |  | Number of `1 / rate` units. |

A DaVinci Resolve effect, as Resolve's OTIO export writes it: in an `Effect`'s `metadata.Resolve_OTIO`, or in a generator's `parameters.Resolve_OTIO` list.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Effect Name` | string | yes |  | Resolve's name for the effect, e.g. `Transform` or `Rich Text`. |
| `Enabled` | boolean |  | `false` | Whether Resolve applies it. |
| `Name` | string |  | `""` | Display name. |
| `Parameters` | array of [ResolveOTIOParameter](#resolveotioparameter) |  |  | The effect's parameters. |
| `Type` | number |  | `0` | Resolve's numeric effect type (e.g. `2` Transform, `24` Rich Text). |

## Tellers effects

Every effect the player renders has the same shape: an `Effect.1` whose `effect_name` is `tellers.ai.<Effect>` and whose parameters are in `metadata["tellers.ai"].parameters`. A bare `<Effect>` name (written before the prefix) is still read. Unknown names are ignored, and an effect with `"enabled": false` is skipped.

```json
{
  "OTIO_SCHEMA": "Effect.1",
  "effect_name": "tellers.ai.Blur",
  "metadata": { "tellers.ai": { "parameters": { "strength": 6 } } }
}
```

The same effect can sit on a clip or a track (applied to each of its clips); clip effects apply first, then the track's. On the stack the player applies only a `MotionBlur` (every clip's default) and `ColorLut`s. Where an effect applies once (`Transform`, `Blend`, `Volume`, ...), the first enabled one wins. Parameters left out take the player's defaults.

| Effect | `effect_name` | Applies to | Parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Blur](#effect-blur) | `tellers.ai.Blur` | video (picture) | `strength`, `quality`, `regions`, `detect` |
| [Pixelate](#effect-pixelate) | `tellers.ai.Pixelate` | video (picture) | `size`, `regions`, `detect` |
| [Adjustment](#effect-adjustment) | `tellers.ai.Adjustment` | video (picture) | `gamma`, `saturation`, `contrast`, `brightness`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `alpha`, `regions`, `detect` |
| [ColorMatrix](#effect-colormatrix) | `tellers.ai.ColorMatrix` | video (picture) | `preset`, `hue`, `amount`, `regions`, `detect` |
| [HslAdjustment](#effect-hsladjustment) | `tellers.ai.HslAdjustment` | video (picture) | `hue`, `saturation`, `lightness`, `colorize`, `amount`, `regions`, `detect` |

| [RGBSplit](#effect-rgbsplit) | `tellers.ai.RGBSplit` | video (picture) | `amount`, `angle`, `regions`, `detect` |
| [ZoomBlur](#effect-zoomblur) | `tellers.ai.ZoomBlur` | video (picture) | `strength`, `centerX`, `centerY`, `innerRadius`, `regions`, `detect` |
| [DropShadow](#effect-dropshadow) | `tellers.ai.DropShadow` | video (picture) | `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `blur`, `alpha`, `color`, `regions`, `detect` |

### Asset references

An effect that loads an asset (a `ColorLut`'s `.cube` file) names it in its `asset_id` parameter, which is what the timeline stores, and the player loads it from its `target_url` parameter. `target_url` is resolved from `asset_id` before playback and stripped before saving, like a media reference's `target_url`; this holds for every effect with an `asset_id`, whatever its name.

A `ColorLut`'s `asset_id` and URL used to be written beside `parameters`, directly in `tellers.ai`, and the URL used to be named `cube_url`; `sanitize` upgrades those forms.

### Follow

A `Transform` that follows a detected subject (the player's `VideoPlayer.followTransform`) keeps its recipe in its `follow` parameter, beside the `x`, `y` and `scale` keyframes computed from it. Playback reads only those keyframes; `follow` is what recomputes them after re-tuning. An item's follow is the one on its first enabled `Transform`.

A follow can be declared before anything is detected, with only `target` and `pick` (and no `x`, `y`, `scale` yet): on load the player detects `target` in the clip, takes the subject at `pick`, computes `region` and the keyframes and reports them (`onFollowResolved`) for the host to save; the host saves it only if the follow did not change during detection. A follow needs `region`, or both `target` and `pick`.

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `region` | the detected region followed, an object of [Mask](#effect-mask) parameters in clip space; required unless `target` and `pick` are given |
| `pick` | `{ "t", "x", "y" }`, plain numbers, all required: where the subject was chosen, at `t` clip seconds and (`x`, `y`) in clip space before crop ((0, 0) the clip's center, ±0.5 its edges); with `target`, enough to detect it again |
| `target` | the detection target it came from: `"faces"` \| `"people"` \| `"animals"` \| `"vehicles"`, or one COCO category: `person`, `bicycle`, `car`, `motorcycle`, `airplane`, `bus`, `train`, `truck`, `boat`, `traffic light`, `fire hydrant`, `stop sign`, `parking meter`, `bench`, `bird`, `cat`, `dog`, `horse`, `sheep`, `cow`, `elephant`, `bear`, `zebra`, `giraffe`, `backpack`, `umbrella`, `handbag`, `tie`, `suitcase`, `frisbee`, `skis`, `snowboard`, `sports ball`, `kite`, `baseball bat`, `baseball glove`, `skateboard`, `surfboard`, `tennis racket`, `bottle`, `wine glass`, `cup`, `fork`, `knife`, `spoon`, `bowl`, `banana`, `apple`, `sandwich`, `orange`, `broccoli`, `carrot`, `hot dog`, `pizza`, `donut`, `cake`, `chair`, `couch`, `potted plant`, `bed`, `dining table`, `toilet`, `tv`, `laptop`, `mouse`, `remote`, `keyboard`, `cell phone`, `microwave`, `oven`, `toaster`, `sink`, `refrigerator`, `book`, `clock`, `vase`, `scissors`, `teddy bear`, `hair drier`, `toothbrush` |
| `detect` | how the detected region looks, kept as given (left out: the player's defaults): the plain numbers `padX`, `padY`, the region's size relative to the detected box; no other key. How well subjects are found (`objectModel`, `faceModel`, `fps`, `width`, `minConfidence`, `maxGap`, `minDuration`) is the player's `detection` option, not the timeline's; `sanitize` drops those keys and `tolerance` from timelines written earlier |
| `fill`, `aspect`, `minZoom`, `maxZoom`, `deadZone`, `zoomDeadZone`, `panSmoothing`, `zoomSmoothing`, `anchorX`, `anchorY`, `hold` | plain numbers: the `followTransform` options of the same names; left out, the player's defaults |

### Attach

A `Transform`'s `attach` keeps its clip (a label, a sticker) on a subject detected in the clip of another video track playing alongside. On load the player detects `target` in the clip of `track` that plays longest alongside this one, takes the subject at `pick` (else the one seen longest) and writes `x` and `y` keyframes (and `opacity`, with `hide`) on the Transform and `region` (and, with `hide`, the clip's own `opacity`) in `attach`, then reports them (`onFollowResolved`, like a follow) for the host to save; the host saves it only if the attach did not change during detection. Playback reads only `x`, `y` and `opacity`; dropping them beside a `region` recomputes them without detection. An item's attach is the one on its first enabled `Transform`. It is meant for a clip centered in the frame (text, full-frame images): Placement, rotation and groups of either clip are not taken into account. Clips with an attach are resolved after the others, so a follow-zoomed source is read with its zoom.

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `track` | required: the video track (its `name`, `id` or `tellers.ai.timeline_id`) whose clip the subject is detected in |
| `target` | what to detect, as a follow's `target` (see [Follow](#follow)); required unless `region` is given |
| `pick` | `{ "t", "x", "y" }`, plain numbers, all required: the subject there, in this clip's seconds and frame coordinates ((0, 0) the frame's center, ±0.5 its edges) |
| `detect` | as a follow's `detect`: `padX`, `padY` |
| `anchorX`, `anchorY` | plain numbers: where this clip's center sits on the subject, as an offset from the subject's center in its widths and heights (`anchorY` -0.5 is its top edge); left out, 0 |
| `smoothing` | plain number: smoothing of the subject's motion, seconds; left out, 0.2 |
| `hide` | boolean: the clip disappears while the subject is unseen, instead of staying where it was last seen; left out, false |
| `opacity` | [animatable](#animatable-parameters): with `hide`, the clip's own opacity, multiplied into the resolved one; written on resolution |
| `region` | the subject's region, an object of [Mask](#effect-mask) parameters in frame coordinates and this clip's seconds; written on resolution |

### Detect

Any filter (an effect taking `regions`) and a `Mask` can declare a subject to detect in their `detect` parameter instead of drawn shapes, e.g. `{ "strength": 40, "detect": { "target": "faces" } }` on a `Blur`. On load the player detects `target` over the clip's source range and resolves the effect: a filter gets `regions` (every subject, or the ones at `pick`), a `Mask` the keyframed shape of one subject (the first one `pick` finds, else the one seen longest) as its `shape`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `opacity`, `points`, keeping its other parameters (`feather`, `invert`, ...). It reports the result (`onDetectResolved`, with the effect's index among all the clip's effects) for the host to save; the host saves it only while the effect and its `detect` did not change during detection. A filter without `regions` or a `Mask` without `x` is unresolved; `detect` stays once resolved, so dropping `regions` (or `x`) detects again. Only clips' effects are resolved, not tracks' or composite clips'.

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `target` | required: what to detect, as a follow's `target` (see [Follow](#follow)) |
| `track` | detect in the clip of this video track (its `name`, `id` or `tellers.ai.timeline_id`) playing longest alongside this clip, instead of in this clip's media: the regions are moved into this clip's time and box, so an overlay's `Mask` with `invert: true` cuts out a subject crossing it; `pick` is then in this clip's seconds and frame coordinates. Those clips are resolved after the others |
| `pick` | `{ "t", "x", "y" }`, as a follow's: only the subject there; or a non-empty list of them, e.g. to blur several chosen faces with one filter (points finding nobody are skipped, two on one subject give it one region; a `Mask` takes the first subject found) |
| `shape` | `"rectangle"` \| `"ellipse"` (the subject's box; faces default to ellipses, others to rounded rectangles) \| `"outline"` (its exact shape, keyframed as a `path`) |
| `padX`, `padY` | the look of the regions, as in a follow's `detect`, here beside `target`; no other key (the detection settings are the player's, see [Follow](#follow)) |

### Track references

A `TrackMatte`'s `track`, a `Transform`'s `attach.track` and a `detect`'s `track` name another track: the video track whose `name` or `tellers.ai.timeline_id` it is, never the effect's own track (the track it is on, or its item is on). A name another video track also carries is ambiguous, so a `tellers.ai.timeline_id` is the safer reference. One that matches no video track does nothing (a `TrackMatte` without `track` reads the track directly above instead), and `validate_timeline` reports it.

`rename_track` points the effects that named a track by its old name at it again: by its new name, or by its `tellers.ai.timeline_id` when it gets no name or one another video track carries. `delete_track` unlinks the effects that named only the deleted track, keeping what they produced: a `TrackMatte` is removed, an `attach` is dropped (its baked `x` and `y` stay), and a `detect` is dropped (its `regions` or shape stay; an unresolved one's effect is removed).

### Animatable parameters

A numeric parameter is either a plain number or keyframes:

```json
{ "keyframes": [ { "t": 0, "v": 0, "ease": "easeOut" }, { "t": 1.5, "v": 8 } ] }
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `t` | Seconds from the start of the clip on the timeline (not source time). |
| `v` | The value at `t`. |
| `ease` | The curve from this keyframe to the next. |

Before the first keyframe the value is the first one's, after the last the last one's. Keyframes are read sorted by `t`.

| `ease` | Curve |
|---|---|
| `linear` | straight line (the default) |
| `hold` | keeps this keyframe's value until the next keyframe |
| `easeIn` | starts slow: `x³` |
| `easeOut` | ends slow: `1 − (1 − x)³` |
| `easeInOut` | slow at both ends (cubic) |
